feature: Reserved class names in the design study
summary: Four reference pages had borrowed a class name the design system already owns, so their own boxes were being laid out by rules nobody wrote for them. The worst case hid a swatch description off the edge of its card. A new check script now fails the moment a page does this again.
setup: Design dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791. Nothing to build. From docs/design/mocks, node shared/check-reserved.mjs is the guard.

try.do: Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/lang-color.html and read the Anatomy swatch card. The token, the sentence and both hexes should all sit inside it.
Compare that card to how it looked before the fix: the sentence was simply gone.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/lang-motion.html and look at the three easing cards. Each rail should be a thin hairline with a dot on it.
Compare to before: each rail sat in a taller padded box with a stray vertical tick at its right end.
Click an easing card. The dot should glide across and stop.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/lang-elevation.html and check the Live examples window: Layers rail on the left, dark canvas on the right.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/video-compositing.html and press Key it. The subject should keep head, hair and shoulders while the green drops out.
Run node shared/check-reserved.mjs from docs/design/mocks and watch it pass; run it with --list to see the 62 names it guards.

evaluate: Does the swatch card now read as one tidy block, or does the description crowd the hexes below it?
Do the easing rails look deliberate at their new height, or too thin to see the dot travel?
Is the guard's rule the right one to gate on, or would you rather it flagged every borrowed name and made someone justify each?
Any of these four pages look worse to you than before, in either theme?
rough: The guard only catches the damaging form: the design system imposing a layout property (grid columns, float, absolute position) on a bare class that a page then styles without redeclaring it. It does not catch a borrowed name that only imposes padding, a border or a glass blur, which is how the motion page's rail broke. I found that one by eye, not by the gate.

Widening the gate to padding and backdrop blur was tried and rejected: it fires on 74 page rules, nearly all of them legitimate refinements of the real component, which would leave a gate nobody can keep green. A follow-up task is filed to triage the rest by hand.

81 pages contain a rule whose key class is a design-system name. That is mostly fine and encouraged (a page tuning a real button is not a collision), so 'no page uses a reserved name' is not the bar; 'no page means something different by one' is.
On lang-elevation the annotation tag 'glass titlebar · elev 2' overlaps the window's own title text. That is pre-existing and unrelated to this fix, but it is worth its own task.
